name: Bunny "Striker" Lee
hook: The most prolific producer in 1970s reggae, whose sheer volume of studio time gave King Tubby the raw material to invent the remix.
blurb: Edward "Bunny" Lee (born Edward O'Sullivan Lee) started in 1962 as a record plugger for Duke Reid's Treasure Isle label before producing his first hit, Roy Shirley's 'Music Field', in 1967. Through the 1970s he was reggae's busiest producer, especially with the singers Johnny Clarke and Cornell Campbell, and he worked constantly with the engineer King Tubby. All that material gave Tubby enough to work with that his dub remixes of Lee's productions turned dub into a genre rather than a one-off trick.

signatureTracks.title: The Gorgon (Cornell Campbell)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A Lee production that launched a wave of like-minded 'Gorgon rock' records, showing how one hit could set a template others copied for years.

signatureTracks.title: None Shall Escape the Judgement (Johnny Clarke)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Part of the Lee/Clarke run of roots hits that, alongside Tubby's dub cuts of the same rhythms, defined mid-1970s Jamaican radio.
